A woman was escorted onto a police vehicle at dawn after her clothing was suspected of carrying seditious intent.

When officers took the woman away, several other officers kept directing reporters to leave, saying "we'll take you to the press area," and pulled the orange cordon toward Ying Wa Street. After the woman boarded the police vehicle, the cordon was taken down.

T-shirt printed with Japanese characters

Ah Wai, a "queue sitter" standing near the woman, said she was wearing a black T-shirt with only Japanese characters printed on it, and he could not understand why police considered her shirt seditious. Ah Wai said he had been to the West Kowloon Court area on Tuesday evening, when he already saw a group queuing. An officer at the time asked him to leave via Ying Wa Street, saying "no queuing allowed tonight," without explaining why. Ah Wai said he understood but did not认同 the Hong Kong Alliance's past stance. As for the verdict, Ah Wai said he was mentally prepared and wanted to "see how the judge writes the judgment."

"Female Long Hair" turned up to queue overnight

Social activist "Female Long Hair" Lui Yuk-lin went to queue last night. She brought only a plastic bag containing her ID card, a pack of tissues and her phone, to avoid police registration and searches.

Lui said she had visited one of the defendants, Lee Cheuk-yan, last week and found him in good spirits. She said Lee had read in the newspapers about her campaigning for workers' rights in hot weather, and told her not to queue, "because he knows there are queue-sitting groups and he doesn't want us to suffer."

Lui said she had visited one of the defendants, Lee Cheuk-yan, last week and found him in good spirits.

Lui, who also works as a cleaner, said she saw rubbish bins outside the court filled to the brim this morning, describing it as "unprecedented." Even after a scavenging granny wheeled away two carts of cardboard, the rubbish situation did not improve. During the interview, an officer approached again and told Lui to leave, saying they would "get someone to clear (the rubbish) later" and "it's no big deal."

Lui, who also works as a cleaner, said she saw rubbish bins outside the court filled to the brim this morning, describing it as "unprecedented."

Suspected queue-sitting group members kept dumping black rubbish bags into nearby bins from the morning. After the bins overflowed into mountains of trash, they dumped more rubbish by the kerb in front of Ying Wa Primary School.

Suspected queue-sitting group dumped rubbish by the kerb and covered it with a tarp.

Suspected queue-sitting group dumps rubbish by the kerb, covered with a tarp

Reporters at the scene observed that people at the head of the queue kept dumping black rubbish bags into nearby bins from the morning. After the bins overflowed into mountains of trash, they dumped more rubbish by the kerb in front of Ying Wa Primary School and covered it with a tarp. One woman wearing a straw hat and mask walked back to the registration area to queue right after dumping the rubbish. A Food and Environmental Hygiene Department-contracted cleaner arrived at around 7am and cleared the rubbish pile together with the scavenging granny. The cleaning woman said, "It only happens when there's a hearing. There isn't any of this when there's no hearing!"

Main court issues 65 tickets; queue-sitting group moves in on Tuesday

The main court only issued 65 tickets, and together with seven extension courts, a total of 553 tickets were issued.

Queue-sitting groups had already moved in outside the court on Tuesday (the 18th), queuing three days in advance. With the thunderstorm warning in effect yesterday morning and a brief heavy downpour in the afternoon, the queue-sitting group laid tarps on the ground. Around 4pm yesterday, some of them were sleeping on the ground, while others took out nail clippers to trim their fingernails outside the court. About 30 people stayed at the scene, and they all had to register their details with the officers stationed there when entering and leaving.

The queue-sitting group moved in on Tuesday; it rained on Thursday, and they laid tarps on the ground.
